title: Does Vinyl Plank Flooring Need to Acclimate Before Installation?
meta: Yes. Most vinyl plank needs 48 hours in the room at 65 to 85 degrees before install; even rigid SPC must reach room temperature. Wills Flooring Edmonds guide.
keywords: does vinyl plank need to acclimate, LVP acclimation time, vinyl plank acclimation temperature, SPC flooring acclimation, luxury vinyl plank expansion and contraction, vinyl plank installation Edmonds

blocks.lead: Yes. Nearly every vinyl plank manufacturer requires the boxes to sit in the room where they will be installed for 48 hours at 65 to 85 degrees, and skipping it is the most common reason a warranty claim gets denied.
blocks.detail: Vinyl does not absorb moisture the way wood does, so this is about temperature, not humidity. A plank that goes down cold expands when the house warms up and peaks at the joints; a plank that goes down hot shrinks and gaps in winter.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether acclimation is a real requirement or a way for installers to pad the schedule. It is real, and Edmonds is a good place to see why. Boxes get delivered to a Seaview rambler on a 40-degree November afternoon and stacked in the garage. Two days later a crew carries them into a 70-degree living room and starts clicking planks together that are still cold in the middle. By February the joints have lifted into little ridges along the hallway. Here is what the instructions actually say, why it matters more for some products than others, and how to do it right in a house that is being lived in.

blocks.text: Why vinyl moves, and why it is not about moisture

items.title: Thermal expansion
items.text: Vinyl and its plasticizers expand when warm and shrink when cool, more than wood does across a plank's length. A 20 ft run of flexible LVP can change by more than 1/4 in between a cold delivery and a heated room. That is the gap or the peak you see later.

items.title: Humidity barely matters to the plank
items.text: Unlike hardwood, vinyl does not take on water from the air. Edmonds waterfront humidity and the Bowl's marine air will not swell a plank. Moisture matters only for what is under the floor: a damp slab or crawlspace subfloor needs a moisture test before any plank goes down.

items.title: SPC is stiffer, not immune
items.text: Rigid stone-plastic core planks move about half as much as flexible vinyl and are marketed as needing little or no acclimation. Read the fine print: most still require the boxes to be at room temperature before installation, and all of them require the room itself to be within range.

items.title: Heat swings after install matter too
items.text: A south-facing Edmonds sunroom or a slider with afternoon sun can heat a plank floor well past 85 degrees. Acclimation cannot fix that; product choice and expansion gaps at the walls do. We flag those rooms at the estimate.

blocks.text: How to acclimate correctly in a house you are living in

items.text: Boxes are delivered and carried into the rooms where they will be installed, not the garage or a covered porch. Our showroom is about 10 minutes from Edmonds, so we can time the delivery to the day.
items.note: A garage in November is 45 degrees. Acclimating there does nothing.

items.text: Cartons lie flat, stacked no more than three or four high, with space between stacks so air reaches every box. Do not stand them on end; planks bow.
The house is at its normal living temperature, 65 to 75 degrees, and stays there. If the heat has been off in an empty house, it goes on now, not the morning of the install.
Subfloor is checked for flatness and, over concrete, for moisture. Planks are pulled from several boxes at once to mix shade variation. Expansion gaps at the walls are set per the product.
The room stays within the same range while the floor settles and, for glue-down, while the adhesive cures. Then live on it normally.

blocks.title: Edmonds condos and vacant homes:
blocks.text: Two situations trip people up. Condos in the Bowl often store deliveries in an unheated garage or storage cage, and estates being prepared for sale often have the heat off. In both cases, the boxes need to move into a heated room two full days before we arrive. We check at the estimate and tell you the delivery date that makes it work.
Questions to ask your installer about acclimation

items.html: Which specific acclimation requirement applies to this plank? The answer should be a number of hours and a temperature range from the manufacturer, not "vinyl does not need it."
When does the material arrive, and where does it sit? In the install rooms, two to three days ahead. If the installer wants to bring it from a cold truck the morning of the job, that is a red flag.
What temperature does the house need to be, and for how long? Before, during and after. Ask what to do if you are between tenants or the home is empty.

Is a subfloor moisture test included over concrete? Acclimation handles the plank; a moisture test handles the slab. Edmonds daylight basements and slab-on-grade additions need it. See why vinyl plank needs a moisture test over concrete.

Who keeps the acclimation record? Delivery date, install date and room temperature. If a plank ever fails, that record is what the manufacturer asks for first. Wills Flooring keeps it with the job file, alongside our 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: How long does vinyl plank flooring need to acclimate?
faq.a: Most manufacturers require 48 hours in the installation room at 65 to 85 degrees; flexible glue-down products often say 48 to 72 hours. Rigid SPC planks sometimes list 24 hours, and a few say none is needed, but even those require the planks and the room to be at normal living temperature before installation begins.

faq.q: Does SPC vinyl plank need to acclimate?
faq.a: Less than flexible vinyl, but usually yes. Stone-plastic core planks move about half as much with temperature, so many brands list 24 hours instead of 48. The room still has to be within the product's temperature range, and boxes coming from a cold garage or truck need time to reach room temperature before they are clicked together.

faq.q: Can I acclimate vinyl plank in the garage?
faq.a: No. Acclimation only works in the room where the floor will be installed, at the temperature the house is normally kept. An Edmonds garage in winter sits in the 40s, so boxes stored there are colder than the room, which is exactly the condition acclimation is meant to prevent. Carry them inside two to three days ahead.

faq.q: Does humidity matter for vinyl plank acclimation?
faq.a: Not for the plank. Vinyl does not absorb moisture from the air, so waterfront humidity or a damp season does not swell it the way it would hardwood or laminate. Humidity does matter for what is under the floor: concrete slabs and crawlspace subfloors need a moisture check before installation regardless of how long the boxes sat.

faq.q: What happens if vinyl plank is installed without acclimating?
faq.a: Planks installed cold expand as the house warms and push against each other, lifting the joints into small ridges called peaking. Planks installed warm shrink in winter and open gaps. Click joints on mismatched-temperature planks may not fully lock. Most manufacturers will also deny a warranty claim if acclimation was skipped.
